# A method of the result that happens to be named StatusCode or Redirect is
# not TemplateData's.
#
# Inside {{with}}, {{range}}, or a partial invoked with a value, dot is
# whatever was selected, so .StatusCode there sets nothing muxt would have
# written. Rejecting it would break a route that works, which is worse than
# the silence err_redirect_with_response_argument.txt exists to fix.
#
# $ is the exception: it is the dot the template started with wherever it is
# written, so $.StatusCode is TemplateData's even inside a with.

muxt generate --use-receiver-type=T
exec go build ./...

-- go.mod --
module server

go 1.24
-- template.gohtml --
{{- define "GET /with-response WithResponse(ctx, response)" -}}
	{{- with .Result -}}
		{{- .StatusCode -}}
		{{- .RedirectSeeOther -}}
	{{- end -}}
	{{- range .Result.Rows -}}
		{{- .StatusCode -}}
	{{- end -}}
	{{- template "row" .Result -}}
{{- end -}}

{{- define "row" -}}
	{{- .StatusCode -}}
{{- end -}}
-- template.go --
package server

import (
	"context"
	"embed"
	"html/template"
	"net/http"
)

//go:embed *.gohtml
var templatesFS embed.FS

var templates = template.Must(template.ParseFS(templatesFS, "*"))

type T struct{}

// Row and Page carry names muxt also uses on TemplateData. They are the
// result's own, and the templates above read them through a rebound dot.
type Row struct {
	StatusCode string
}

type Page struct {
	StatusCode       string
	RedirectSeeOther string
	Rows             []Row
}

func (T) WithResponse(ctx context.Context, response http.ResponseWriter) Page { return Page{} }
